# Relift technical reference

Relift is a GPL-3.0-or-later Rust workspace with a CLI and a Tauri desktop frontend. It scans raw images and operating-system raw device paths using read-only source access. Recovery output must pass destination-separation checks.

## Interfaces

The CLI supports scanning, recovery, imaging, device listing, candidate listing, reports, diagnostics, and shell completions. Consult docs/src/CLI.md for exact flags, JSON shapes, and exit codes. The desktop GUI supports source selection, scan progress, candidate filtering, metadata preview, and recovery. Imaging, report export, and checkpoint resume remain CLI-only. Scans resume at volume boundaries; imaging resumes from durable prefix checkpoints. Imaging does not retry unreadable sectors.

## Data and sessions

Sessions use a JSON header and JSONL records. A completed session can be reused. An interrupted scan can be resumed with `relift scan --resume`; the source size and fingerprint are revalidated and completed volumes are skipped. Interrupted imaging can be resumed with `relift image --resume`; a JSONL map records durable prefix hashes. It does not provide a bad-sector map or multi-pass retry.

## Evidence boundaries

FAT, exFAT, NTFS, and ext2/3/4 have deterministic synthetic fixture coverage with byte-exact SHA-256 recovery checks. HFS+, APFS, Btrfs, and XFS have deterministic probe fixtures, but metadata-based deleted-file recovery on those filesystems is experimental and not end-to-end validated. Carving registers 153 format identifiers, including marker-only entries; only formats with structural validators can emit candidates, and their maturity varies. See docs/src/formats.md. No real physical drive or representative real-media corpus has been validated.

## Operational safety

Never write to the source device. Verify source and destination are different physical volumes, run recovery with dry-run first, and ask the human before accessing physical media. Stop using a drive after deletion. Do not treat SMART, TRIM, or device health as detected by Relift.

## Build

Requires Rust 1.90 or newer. GUI development requires Node.js 22.17 or newer.

    cargo build --release --workspace
    cargo test --workspace --all-targets
    cd crates/relift-gui
    npm ci
    npm run check
    npm run tauri build

For current support, release status, and evidence, use docs/src/support-matrix.md, docs/src/GAP_REPORT.md, and docs/src/VERIFICATION.md.
